analysis.title: Qnity (Q): Strong quarter with guidance raise and improved margin execution - Buy
key_insights: Qnity reported 3Q26 revenue of $1.56bn, above GS at $1.48bn and the Street (Visible Alpha) at $1.49bn. Revenue grew 22% YoY organic.
Semiconductor Technologies revenue was $797mn vs GS $759mn and Street $767mn. Interconnect Solutions revenue was $759mn vs GS $719mn and Street $724mn.
Adjusted EBITDA margin was 32.3% vs GS 30.4% and Street 30.1%. Adjusted pro forma EPS was $1.46 vs GS $1.22 and Street $1.19.

Management cited advanced logic and DRAM fab utilization in the high-80% range. Mature logic utilization improved from the low-80% range last quarter to low-to-mid 80% in 3Q, with further QoQ improvement expected into 2027.

Consumer electronics demand remains soft, reflected in seasonal 4Q guidance. Growth there stays positive on premium smartphones and content wins, and management said AI infrastructure strength more than offsets the weakness.

Interconnect Solutions revenue rose 30% YoY on advanced packaging, advanced interconnects (especially AI PCBs) and thermal management. Thermal management sales grew more than 50% YoY in 3Q, consistent with 2Q.

Adjusted pro-forma operating EBITDA margin expanded about 330bps YoY. Gross margin expanded about 100bps and beat GS after a miss last quarter. Management expects EBITDA margins to keep rising, with ICS offering the most incremental upside, and expects raw material and logistics inflation to be largely offset by pricing with some timing variability.

FY26 guidance was raised above the Street. Revenue midpoint is $5.80bn vs prior GS $5.71bn and Street $5.65bn. Adjusted EPS guidance of $4.95-$5.05 compares with GS $4.65 and Street $4.55. Adjusted operating EBITDA midpoint is $1.795bn vs GS $1.73bn and Street $1.71bn.
GS raised EPS estimates by about 10% on average: 2026E $5.10 (from $4.65), 2027E $6.75 (from $6.00), 2028E $8.20 (from $7.15).
GS kept its 12-month price target at $175, based on 32x P/E on normalized EPS of $5.50. Price was $118.89, implying 47.2% upside. Bull case value is $202 and bear case $103.
Key downside risks are a slowdown in wafer starts across DRAM, NAND and foundry/logic, tighter tariffs and export restrictions, and additional PFAS litigation liabilities.

GS expects the stock to eventually trade higher. It says positioning was constructive going into the print, helped by strong results from Entegris and expectations of a broad wafer start recovery in 2026.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 revenue, margin and EPS beat GS and the Street, and FY26 guidance was raised above consensus. GS raised EPS estimates by about 10% and kept the $175 target.

sector_views.rationale: AI/HPC and advanced packaging tailwinds plus a cyclical recovery in wafer starts, particularly in trailing-edge and analog markets, support volume and revenue upside.
